name: Dark Spring Green
lede: Dark Spring Green is a deep, slightly cool green named for the fresh growth of early spring, catalogued as a darker companion to a lighter Spring Green on the web's X11 color list.

sections.title: A season's green, by way of X11
sections.body: The word points to the pale, slightly yellow green of new spring leaves, the sense the lighter Spring Green already carries on the same list, though our sources give no exact year for when the X11 extended color names first wrote either one down [1]. Wikipedia's own color-name pages cite the X11 and web lists as the source for Dark Spring Green rather than a dictionary or an atlas [1]. There is no separate Spring Green entry in our own name set, so the word's nature sense has to carry the whole explanation [1]. Its nearest named neighbors on file are [[emerald-green]] and [[cadmium-green]], both almost the same at 2.5 to 2.7 CIEDE2000 units [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this green, as photographed, in 22 of 23,781 paintings, 0.09 percent, rarer than 66 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, 7 of 1,674 paintings from that century, 5.1 times the expected rate [3]. The earliest dated match is a Tibetan *Tathagata Buddha* painting from 1860; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone, in 33 percent of its 12 strongest matches [3].

origin.named_after: the fresh green of spring growth, one shade darker than a Spring Green our data does not separately list
origin.first_recorded: undocumented; Wikipedia cites the X11 and web color lists
